questions.question: What color is a warning sign, and what color are its symbols?

options.text: Yellow with black symbols
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Hold the handgrips tight and speed up to get past the hazard.
Zigzag across the surface.
Ride on the shoulder instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding
When you slow down where drivers don't expect it
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your turn signals don't work

questions.correctAnswerText: When you slow down where drivers don't expect it
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see. Flash your brake light before slowing down in places drivers may not expect it, like the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to wobble or shake?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Brakes that are not working properly
A balanced load
Excessive wind

questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Other drivers can see you as easily as other vehicles
Other drivers can't see you
You don't need to help other drivers see you
You should ride offensively

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles. Assume other drivers don't see you. Ride defensively to stay safe.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up
Sit far back so you can keep your arms straight
Keep your knees away from the gas tank
Drag your feet on the ground

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly
Use it only on slippery roads
It is less effective than the rear brake
It is safe to use if you use it properly

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it properly
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when slowing or stopping. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, and it is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These are regulatory signs that tell drivers what rules to follow.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, which brake should you use?

options.text: The brake of the tire that is not flat
The brake of the tire that is flat
Both brakes
Neither brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake of the tire that is not flat
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat (if you are sure which one that is).

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright and rise off your seat so your knees can absorb the impact. Just before contact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: When should you leave a larger space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny outside.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normally good. Leave more space when conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it during the day and night.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes to slow or stop?

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Rarely.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together to get the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: How can you stop other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left part of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to reduce empty space on both sides of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: How much maintenance does a motorcycle need compared to a car?

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.
Pre-ride checks should only be done by a mechanic.
Service should only be done at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle more often than a car. Do a complete check before every ride.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time. Apply them firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Where is the horn button located on most motorcycles?

options.text: Near the left handlebar
Near the right handlebar
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride. The horn button is usually near the left handlebar.

questions.question: How do you get maximum braking power on a straight road?

options.text: Using only the rear brake.
Using only the front brake.
Using both brakes without locking the wheels.
Using both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what should you use?

options.text: High beam headlight
Low beam headlight
No lights
Switch between low and high beams

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams near other vehicles, as they reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day
Wear dark clothes
Keep your headlight on at all times
Ride in the right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times
questions.explanation: To be more visible, keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright or reflective clothing and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to maximize the surface of the road
It limits your escape routes
It allows you to communicate with one another
It makes it easier for other motorists to pass

questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another rider. This limits both riders' options to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do to improve safety when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed
Reduce your speed
Use your high beam headlight when possible
Increase your following distance

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use high beams when not near other vehicles. Watch vehicles ahead of you for clues about the road. Their lights help show what is ahead.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer
The front tire provides power, so you lose acceleration
The flat tire will shake the bike, making mirrors hard to use
You will not be able to use the brake

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your steering. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.
